questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, it was definitely Paris as a city and France in general that was the principal reason for my exchange and not the university. I didn't know much about Panthéon-Assas.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy and often you needed to contact the administration to get your needed information. As there were some problems they would answer quite slowly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an intro meeting and then you could contact the administration.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't easy as I had to find it by myself. I ended up living in a Cité Universitaire which was brilliant but it was very random that I found it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I would absolutely recommend living in Cité Universitaire! You need to apply (if you're danish) through La Fondation Danoise:
https://www.fondationdanoise.org/
If you're  not danish then I think it's the same concept where you'll apply through the house you come from. Then afterwards you shall continue through
https://www.ciup.fr/
- but i'm pretty sure the house representing your house will guide you.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It wasn't too difficult, but the lack of updated and correct course description made the process difficult concerning the pre-approval process. Also, at my host-university (Københavns Universitet), they were very strict and that really made it difficult to get the courses I wanted. The other Erasmus students didn't have the same problem.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to send the course description, ECTS, exam description etc. several times through different formulas.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Contacting my administration, contacting the Paris administration and some guides.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There were many courses that I wasn't allowed to get - I think I was refused 50 % as they weren't strictly discussing typical law courses. I didn't get this, as it is possible to get courses on other facultiies in Denmark and a lot of courses on law are different from traditional law courses when you choose optional courses - but very important that they are good old conservative law courses when you're on exchange!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing really - just expect that you'll have to choose law courses and that you will probably get a couple of french courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level wasn't toon high compared to the level we're used to in Copenhagen but the teaching and studying method is so different in Paris so that it will challenge you a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very conservative and primarily big amphithéatre (audiotorium) courses where they speak for 2-3 hours and you don't interact with the teacher.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
History of European Legal Systems
History of the European Legal Systems
European Law 
Introduction au droit de la communication
Philosophy of Law
Droit de l'union européenne 2
Philosophie du droit et de la justice
International investment Law

I also had french courses but I wasn't allowed the ECTS that I received for them in Paris (4,5 ECTS).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take all the english ones as they are easier and more suited for Erasmsus (they are less harsh on you as they don't expect an expert in the french method. Check the exam if it's released (wasn't the case when I went). Otherwise just take the courses that you find intereseting but not too difficult and not master courses (no extra exam try if you fail)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At the panthéon-assas I would give it 1, but as the cité universitaire it was incredibly nice! So if youn live there I'd say 5 stars!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're under 26 years old almost all museums are free and a lot of student prices.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever you like as Paris has most activities!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Again, as you like. However, if you like visiting other cities then reserve a ticket for the TGV (fast train) some weeks before doing a trip and you'll quickly and very comfortably. I went to Marseille and loved it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was alright - the Parisians are a lot like people from Copenhagen - difficult to engage with, but if you live in the cité universitaire you'll have a social basis there and then you try to meet some real parisians and hang out with the Erasmus people if it clicks.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Nothing other than what you've learned from home.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are more direct in the trains and they are more loud and sometimes annoying - you'll get used to it. Also, you have to be more formal when talking to teachers and authorities etc. VERY IMPORTANT to say "bonjour/bonsoir" when you enter in cafés, shops, bars and clubs or they'll be annoyed with you - and I guess it's fair enough.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Outgoing and laissez-faire culture. Some much life in the city concerning culture, cafés and bars everyday outside and inside - so nice!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Do you want to go to Paris because it's a nice city? Consider whether it's worth it as they are more harsh in Paris towards Erasmus students. If you love Paris or just wanna experience the culture badly then it's definetly worth it. If you're in between two then choose the other. 
2) You gain a lot by studying french before coming! However don't stress about it it'll be alright.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Idk.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and the cultural experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being a new place with so little help and support. Also, being confronted with the language barrier even though I had a pretty good level of French.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
